A1.justification: Both PDFs describe M-MAD and support a complete comparison, including their appendices. Retained text, equations, tables and figures can be reliably matched across the expanded prompt appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original WMT23 evaluations, ablations and analyses in Sections 3–4, plus HE-EN results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main evaluations, ablations and appendix results.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the three-stage framework, four evaluation dimensions, two-agent debates and MQM scoring. New Figures 7–9 disclose prompts for the existing procedure without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both use WMT23 ZH-EN, EN-DE and HE-EN evaluations and WMT22 few-shot demonstrations. The newly displayed examples document existing coverage rather than establish additional datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark, error-span and debate-framework comparisons, including GEMBA-MQM, EAPrompt and the Liang and Khan debate approaches.

E3.justification: Both retain the 45-system, 68,130-segment evaluation, the same meta-evaluation metrics, GPT-4o mini, temperature zero and four-shot setup. No revised experimental protocol is reported.

E4.justification: The stage ablations, error-span and score-distribution analyses, debate comparisons, round sensitivity and case studies are unchanged. The added appendix examples are prompt demonstrations.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and seed information, statistical testing and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. The revision adds no statistical estimation procedures or uncertainty displays.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and qualitative outcomes are retained, including M-MAD's Meta score of 0.814 in Table 2 and HE-EN Meta score of 0.787 in Table 9. Added demonstration annotations are not new evaluation results.

T1.justification: The formal agent/debate setup in Section 2.2 and MQM scoring equation (1) are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same novelty, performance and framework-design claims, without substantive strengthening or narrowing.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, interpretations of gold-annotation errors, and limitations concerning model costs and homogeneous agent groups are unchanged in Section 4, Appendix E and Limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds stage prompt templates, debater initialization, consensus-checking and synthesis instructions in Figures 7–9. It also documents ZH-EN terminology/style examples and all four EN-DE example groups, substantially expanding reproducibility information beyond v1's two M-MAD example groups.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and research positioning in Section 5 are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first two authors exchange order, Appendix B cross-references change, and retained example captions specify Stage 1. Main prose and section organization remain intact. The revised EAPrompt reference incorrectly points to Figure 9 instead of Figure 6.

P2.justification: The appendix adds three stage-prompt figures (7–9) and six demonstration figures (12–17), substantially expanding its visual documentation. Earlier Figures 7–8 are retained as Figures 10–11 and redistributed among the additions. Main figures and tables remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added stage prompts and demonstrations make the existing method easier to inspect and reproduce. This benefit is limited by the incorrect EAPrompt cross-reference and erroneous example spans: 'merchants' in Figure 13 and 'wird' in Figure 16 are absent from their corresponding translations. Overall, v2 offers a modest documentation improvement with unchanged scientific evidence.
